items.title: Australian scientist ignites war over the world's longest lives
items.description: When an Australian academic began questioning the science behind "Blue Zones", he sparked a bitter battle in the field of longevity research.

items.title: Car maker admits selling wrong year vehicles to 1,200 people
items.description: More than 1,200 customers who bought electric and hybrid cars from Chinese maker BYD will be offered a full refund after the company admitted to selling them vehicles from the wrong year.

items.title: Curbing well-off taxpayers' access to key programs could save billions
items.description: Curbing access to the child care subsidy, parental leave pay, aged care and pensions for some of the most well-off taxpayers would free up about $21 billion a year, a new report says.

items.title: Live: Spain strikes late to seal semi berth after Belgium keeper howler
items.description: Spain will face France in a World Cup semifinal after beating Belgium 2-1 thanks to a late Mikel Merino goal. Follow live.

items.title: The World Cup just had one of its hottest matches
items.description: A 38-degree Celsius evening match has raised fresh questions about how football manages heat in a warming world.

items.title: British ex-minister allegedly murdered
items.description: The 78-year-old, who found fame as a Strictly Come Dancing contestant when she left office, was found dead at her home having sustained serious injuries.

items.title: Trump wanted NATO to be about him. Instead, it was about everyone else
items.description: Trump demanded to be the centre of attention. But the more significant news out of NATO was really about everyone else.

items.title: What inquiry revealed about social media giants and online 'Jew hatred'
items.description: It was gloves off at the royal commission on antisemitism this week, with Elon Musk's X bearing the brunt of the inquiry's frustrations with obstructive social media giants.

items.title: King and Queen host Harry, Meghan and children at private residence
items.description: The royal couple hosted the duke and duchess and their children Archie and Lilibet at a country retreat.

items.title: Hinch revealed a scenario that seemed too crazy to be true — but he was right
items.description: Derryn Hinch was not a hero to every survivor of sexual abuse, but in the decades when they lacked allies, he was their fiercest public advocate.

items.title: A 'well-known' risk caused Telstra's outage. Why did it get caught out?
items.description: Telstra faces an outage investigation as an expert says legal gaps may let the telco off the hook.

items.title: Police release video of killer Bradley Murdoch filmed days before his death
items.description: In never-before-seen footage of police questioning Bradley John Murdoch in his final days, the notorious murderer repeatedly tells officers he "knows nothing" about the location of Peter Falconio's remains.

items.title: 'Incredible musician': Cold Chisel saxophonist Andy Bickers dies
items.description: Cold Chisel saxophone player Andy Bickers has died after "hard fought battle with cancer", the band has announced.

items.title: How Jessica Mauboy is marking NAIDOC Week with her daughter
items.description: From singing to her daughter to laughing with her aunties, Jessica Mauboy is all about family. This NAIDOC Week, the star is sharing the music, culture and community she grew up with in a whole new way.

items.title: Hollywood's biggest names can't say no to Nolan
items.description: Christopher Nolan and the cast of the highly anticipated The Odyssey sit down with ABC News Breakfast to talk about the upcoming film.

items.title: ABC 5050 quiz: Testing your knowledge of Jurassic Park, the Scottish play and Wimbledon fruit
items.description: Each question in the ABC 50/50 quiz has only two options: one is right, the other is wrong. But there's a catch.

items.title: Creator of Cape Fear TV show probably first heard about it from The Simpsons
items.description: The 1957 book The Executioners has been made into two movies and an iconic episode of The Simpsons. It's now a TV show, starring Amy Adams, Patrick Wilson and Javier Bardem.

items.title: Hewitt qualifies for Wimbledon boys' final, first Aussie since de Minaur
items.description: Cruz Hewitt continues his dominant run at Wimbledon, keeping his straight sets record intact en-route to the boys' final.

items.title: Sinner, Zverev to face off in blockbuster Wimbledon final
items.description: British wildcard Arthur Fery's bid to make Wimbledon history has ended after he was knocked out by Alexander Zverev, who will face off against reigning champion Jannik Sinner in the final.

items.title: The 99-year-old Victorian mechanic still working six days a week
items.description: Ray Gloster has been a mechanic for 83 years and counting, and at 99, he might be on the verge of a world record.

items.title: Hobart's Mona announces plans to set up art museum in Thailand
items.description: Museum of Old and New Art founder David Walsh signs an agreement to set up MONA Bangkok in Thailand. Mona says the new iteration will be "unconventional and unique", like its Hobart museum.

items.title: Outback towns welcome grey nomads after slow start to tourism season
items.description: Grey nomads are giving a much-needed boost to outback Queensland towns over the winter tourism season, but locals say more visitors are needed to fuel economic growth.

items.title: Handmade quilts babies 'will have for life' wrap them in culture
items.description: Beautiful Indigenous-themed quilts have been made by a group of women for a NAIDOC Week baby celebration on Worimi country, linking cultures and generations.

items.title: Grandmother's 32-hour bus 'adventure' home after train shutdown
items.description: A bus trip that should have taken only 13 hours turned into a 32-hour interstate marathon for a Torquay grandmother due to this week's Telstra outage, while there is still no date for when Victorian passengers can claim compensation from V/Line.

items.title: 'Healing from trauma': The fashion show not about the dresses
items.description: Esperance Nyirabarahinyuza survived the Rwandan genocide. Now, she is helping more than 100 refugee and migrant women in Logan rediscover confidence, community and belonging, one conversation at a time.
